text:
aj: heads-up — customer 'cardinal' asked for a timeline to move their rerank pipeline from 512 -> 768 embeddings. They want low risk and a migration plan. anyone have a PRD or checklist? cc @maria @lee

maria: quick take — dim change is a breaking index format. options: reindex (safe), projection/padding (fast, lossy), or side-by-side indexing + per-query routing. each has tradeoffs on cost and quality.

lee: agree with maria. breakdown: 1) reindex all docs (golden, expensive), 2) projection matrix (train a 512->768 mapper), 3) store dual embeddings during transition and route queries accordingly.

sophia: note: projection prototype we ran on a small corpus gave ~0.86 Pearson on pairwise similarity vs native 768, but ranking delta varied by query type. it helped some queries, hurt others.

aj: for the PRD we should capture acceptance criteria + rollout plan. initial thoughts: - quality gate: recall@10 drop <= 1% absolute, nDCG change <= 0.01 - perf gate: p95 latency increase <= 5ms - cost gate: reindexing cost estimate and budget cap - compatibility: SDK must expose embedding_dim and model_version in responses

maria: + monitoring signals: delta_cosine_histogram, recall@k (sampled eval set), nDCG, embedding_norm_shift, query-term coverage. also add alarms for >2% regressions over 1h.

lee: for batching semantics — cross-batch padding and kv-cache shapes are a separate concern for the runtime. but for embedding generation the only subtlety is consistent normalization: if we switch to L2-normalized output at 768 and customers rely on raw vectors, scores shift. so PRD needs a normalization compatibility section.

sophia: important edge-case: old reranker ops that assume fixed-dim metadata tags. migration could break downstream pipelines if they validate dim == 512. need a soft-fail mode that logs but doesn't hard-error.

aj: put a tiny acceptance snippet here to paste into PRD:```
Acceptance criteria:
- Sampled eval (5k queries) shows recall@10 delta <= 1% absolute vs current 512 baseline
- nDCG@10 delta <= 0.01
- Cosine similarity distribution shift mean <= 0.02 and stdev within historical range
- Production canary (1% traffic) shows no >2% regression over 24h
- SDK surfaces embedding_dim and model_tag, and server returns compatible content-type errors for mismatched dims
```

maria: rollout proposal: phase 0 = projection POC on dev index (no customer traffic). phase 1 = internal canary (0.1% traffic) + telemetry. phase 2 = opt-in seed customers (Cardinal) at 1%. phase 3 = wider roll with dual-index support. fallback is to route to 512 index if delta > threshold.

lee: ops checklist: reindex job template, estimate for 100M docs, cost per hour, cancellation hooks, indexes TTL for rollback. also a migration-safety script to compute per-document projection error distribution so we can flag docs that project poorly.

infra-bot: deploy/infra: canary env `embed-768-canary` created (id: canary-20240422-7).

aj: decision proposal: short-term path = projection + 1% seeded canary for affected customers who accept opt-in. long-term: provide a reindex tool and recommend full reindex for customers who want deterministic parity.

sophia: tests needed: unit tests for projection matrix, integration test comparing top-k for 5k queries, stress test for batch generation with mixed dims, e2e runbook for rollback.

maria: i'll draft a 1-pager PRD with the above and put in the product backlog. target: draft by Mon EOD. lee — can you spike projection POC by Wed? sophia — can you run the 5k eval when lee has outputs?

aj: thanks. owners set. tagging this for prioritization in next roadmap sync — we need to decide whether this is priority-high (customer SLA) or medium (opt-in). :thumbsup:

lee: fyi — projection approach will require us to store the projection matrix version in model metadata so we can reproduce results.

aj: perfect. will link the PRD draft here when ready.

maria: added to my queue.

lee: adding `rerank-dim-migration` to our infra board with the initial estimate.

sophia: if anyone wants the quick eval script i used, ping me and i'll drop it in the repo.

aj: end — thanks everyone!
